channel.title: Uichan Lee — Posts
channel.description: Notes on data science, econometrics, machine learning, and programming by Uichan Lee.

item.title: 반도체 산업 동향의 이해
item.description: 반도체의 정의, 제품의 종류와 특징, 반도체 산업의 구조와 글로벌 반도체 시장

item.title: DL 1 - Introduction
item.description: What is Deep Learning? Layer, Activation Function, Loss Function

item.title: Econometrics Overview
item.description: A capstone review of ENVECON C118: how causal economic questions are answered with potential outcomes, RCTs, OLS, DiD, IV, and RD — and the assumptions each design relies on.

item.title: Fuzzy RD
item.description: When crossing the cutoff only changes the probability of treatment rather than fully determining it, fuzzy RD combines the RD design with an IV-style adjustment.

item.title: Estimating RD in Practice
item.description: How RD can fail (a second policy at the cutoff, or unit manipulation of the running variable), and how to estimate RD with local polynomial regression and bandwidth choice.

item.title: Regression Discontinuity
item.description: Regression discontinuity exploits sharp cutoffs in a running variable to identify causal effects — units just above and below the threshold are comparable in everything except treatment.

item.title: LATE ≠ ATE
item.description: Even with a valid instrument, IV recovers the LATE — the average effect for compliers — not the ATE for the whole population.

item.title: Intro to Functions
item.description: Writing functions in R — the function() syntax, the parts of a function, and how to work with their arguments.

item.title: IV and Regression | From One Instrument to Many
item.description: Estimating the IV coefficient as the ratio of the reduced form to the first stage, and generalizing from a single instrument to multiple instruments via 2SLS.

item.title: Instrumental Variables
item.description: When treatment isn't as-good-as random and DiD's parallel trends fails, instrumental variables offer another path: find a Z that exogenously shocks the confounded X.

item.title: Iterations and Loops
item.description: Three iterative paradigms in R — for, while, and repeat — for performing a procedure multiple times.

item.title: The Parallel Trends Assumption (Revisited)
item.description: Revisiting the parallel trends assumption that underpins DiD, how to test it with pre-trends, and why panel regressions need clustered standard errors.

item.title: DiD with Multiple Time Periods
item.description: Extending DiD beyond simple before/after with longer panel data — testing pre-trends, estimating dynamic effects, and handling staggered treatment timing.

item.title: Expressions and Conditionals
item.description: R code is composed of a series of expressions, which can be grouped and controlled with conditionals like if/else.

item.title: Types of Ensemble Regression
item.description: Ensemble methods combine multiple base learners — bagging, random forests, and boosting — to reduce variance or bias and improve predictive accuracy.

item.title: ML/DS Fundamentals
item.description: ML/DS 면접 대비 핵심 개념 정리 — 확률·통계 기본, bias-variance tradeoff, 손실 함수와 평가 지표, gradient descent, 회귀 모델, 트리 계열 모델, PCA까지.

item.title: DiD in Practice: Currie and Walker (2011)
item.description: Applying the DiD framework to study the effect of E-ZPass adoption on infant health near toll plazas, with fixed effects to control for unobserved confounders.

item.title: Difference-in-Differences
item.description: The DiD estimator is the difference between the treatment group's pre/post change and the control group's pre/post change — valid under the parallel trends assumption.

item.title: Natural Experiments: Difference-in-Differences
item.description: When randomization isn't possible, natural experiments exploit real-world events that assign treatment 'as if' randomly. Difference-in-differences uses changes over time in a control group to construct the counterfactual.

item.title: F-Test | Hedonic Regression | Adjusted R^2
item.description: F-tests check whether a group of variables jointly affects the outcome. We also cover hedonic regression and why adjusted R² is preferred for comparing models.

item.title: `ggplot2`
item.description: An introduction to ggplot2 in R: geoms, aesthetics, mappings, and scales for layered, declarative data visualization.

item.title: `tidyverse`
item.description: An overview of the tidyverse ecosystem (readr, dplyr, tidyr, ggplot2, etc.) and tibbles — an enhanced, safer version of the data frame.

item.title: Inference
item.description: An estimate by itself doesn't tell us much. Statistical inference — t-statistics, p-values, and confidence intervals — lets us ask whether a result could have arisen by chance.

item.title: RCT | Sample Means | Hypothesis Testing | Sampling Distributions of beta hat
item.description: Randomized controlled trials solve the omitted-variable bias problem. We also introduce hypothesis testing and the sampling distribution of β̂.

item.title: Importing Tables | Data Frames
item.description: Reading plain-text tables (delimited and fixed-width) into R, and working with the resulting data frames.

item.title: Confidence Intervals
item.description: When omitted variable bias is unavoidable, signing the bias can still give useful upper or lower bounds. We also build confidence intervals around our coefficient estimates.

item.title: Adding Variables to Regression
item.description: Three cases when adding a regressor: an irrelevant variable, a relevant but uncorrelated variable, and a relevant variable correlated with existing regressors — each with different implications for bias and variance.

item.title: The Limits of Simple Linear Regression | Multiple Regression | Choosing what goes into the regression
item.description: Simple linear regression struggles to draw ceteris paribus conclusions. Multiple regression adds controls — but which variables should we include?

item.title: Regression Recap
item.description: A recap of simple linear regression, goodness-of-fit (R²), log/linear transformations, and the assumptions underlying OLS.

item.title: Matrices | Lists
item.description: Matrices are vectors with a dim attribute, and lists can hold mixed types — two foundational containers in R.

item.title: Regression Model
item.description: The simple linear regression model y = β₀ + β₁x + u — its components, assumptions, and what the coefficients mean.

item.title: Parameter, Estimator, Estimand, Estimate
item.description: Defining the four key concepts — parameter, estimand, estimator, and estimate — and how identification differs from inference.

item.title: Vectors | Factors
item.description: Vectors are the most basic data structure in R — atomic and list flavors. Factors store categorical data with predefined levels.

item.title: Parameters, Estimands, and Estimators
item.description: Distinguishing inference (learning estimands from estimators) from identification (learning parameters from estimands) — two separate steps in econometric reasoning.

item.title: Joint and Conditional Distributions
item.description: Many interesting economic questions involve features of the joint distribution of two or more random variables, along with conditional distributions and independence.

item.title: Getting Started with R
item.description: Why R? An introduction to R for statistical computing and data analysis.

item.title: Random Variables and Distributions
item.description: A random variable is a numerical summary of a random process. We define CDFs, PMFs, PDFs, and distinguish empirical from true distributions.

item.title: What is Econometrics?
item.description: Econometric questions come in three flavors: descriptive, causal, and forecasting. The hardest are causal — because we only ever observe a sample, and selection bias can distort what we infer.

item.title: Clustering | Principal Component Analysis (PCA) | Singular Value Decomposition (SVD)
item.description: K-Means is the most popular clustering approach. We also cover PCA and SVD for dimensionality reduction and uncovering structure in high-dimensional data.

item.title: Logistic Regression II
item.description: Turning logistic regression's probabilities into class predictions via a decision boundary, and evaluating classifiers with accuracy, precision, recall, and ROC curves.

item.title: Radix Sort
item.description: Sorting stability preserves the order of equivalent items. Radix sort exploits this — sorting digit by digit with a stable subroutine — to beat the O(N log N) comparison lower bound.

item.title: Logistic Regression I
item.description: Moving from linear regression to classification: logistic regression models the probability of a binary outcome with the sigmoid function.

item.title: Insertion Sort (In-place) | Quicksort
item.description: Insertion sort is extremely fast on nearly-sorted arrays (few inversions). Quicksort partitions around a pivot for an expected O(N log N) sort.

item.title: SQL II
item.description: Continuing SQL with GROUP BY, aggregate functions, primary and foreign keys, and a deeper look at SQL's declarative style.

item.title: Tries | Basic Sorts (Sorting I)
item.description: When keys are strings, tries store each letter as a node in a tree for fast lookups. We also begin sorting with selection sort, heapsort, and merge sort.

item.title: Parameter Inference and the Bootstrap | SQL
item.description: The bootstrap resamples our data with replacement to quantify uncertainty around an estimate, enabling confidence intervals and hypothesis testing. We also introduce SQL for working with databases.

item.title: Hash Tables
item.description: Hash tables convert data into a hash code, reduce it to an index, and store items in buckets — yielding θ(1) average-case lookups when items are well-spread.

item.title: Random Variables
item.description: A random variable represents the outcome of a random event. We cover discrete vs. continuous RVs, expectation, variance, and how they connect to statistical inference.

item.title: Spanning Trees | Directed Acyclic Graphs
item.description: A spanning tree of an undirected graph connects all vertices with no cycles. We cover MSTs with Prim's algorithm and explore DAGs and topological sort.

item.title: Batch, mini-batch, and stochastic gradient descent | Feature Engineering | Defining Distributions
item.description: Mini-batch and stochastic gradient descent approximate the full gradient using random samples, trading exactness for faster, cheaper updates per epoch.

item.title: Trees and Traversals | Graph Traversals and Implementations
item.description: Tree traversals (level, pre, in, post-order), then graph traversals (BFS, DFS) and common adjacency representations.

item.title: `sklearn` and Gradient Descent
item.description: Fitting linear regression with sklearn, then learning gradient descent: from intuition (path of least resistance) to learning rates, convexity, and high-dimensional gradients.

item.title: Binary Search Tree | B-Trees | Left Leaning Red-Black Trees (LLRBs) | Priority Queues and Heaps
item.description: From BSTs to self-balancing B-trees and left-leaning red-black trees, plus priority queues backed by heaps.

item.title: Ordinary Least Squares (OLS)
item.description: OLS combines multiple linear regression with mean squared error. We derive the closed-form solution by projecting Y onto the column space of the design matrix X.

item.title: Asymptotic II | Asymptotic III | Extends, Sets, Maps, and BSTs
item.description: Big-O as 'less than or equal' (vs. Big-Theta's 'equals'), recursive runtime analysis, and an introduction to inheritance, Sets, Maps, and BSTs.

item.title: Simple Linear Regression
item.description: The regression line is the unique straight line that minimizes the mean squared error of estimation among all straight lines.

item.title: Asymptotic I
item.description: Characterizing the runtimes of functions with Big-Theta notation — a first look at asymptotic analysis.

item.title: Visualization II
item.description: Moving from univariate to bivariate and multivariate visualizations: scatter plots, hex plots, and techniques for handling overplotting.

item.title: Method Overloading in Java
item.description: Java allows multiple methods with same name, but different parameters.

item.title: Regular Expressions (Regex)
item.description: Canonicalization converts data into a standard form, often using regex (regular expressions) to match patterns within strings.

item.title: Doubly Linked List
item.description: Adding a .last pointer speeds up .addLast and .getLast, but not .removeLast. The doubly linked list with backward links solves this.

item.title: Grouping
item.description: The split-apply-combine paradigm in pandas: groupby() splits a DataFrame into subframes, and agg() applies aggregations to each group.

item.title: Java Collections and Linked Lists
item.description: Java arrays are fixed-size, but Lists, Sets, and Maps are resizable. We also explore primitive vs. reference types and build a singly linked list with a sentinel node.

item.title: Pandas
item.description: An introduction to pandas: Series as 1-D labeled arrays, DataFrames as 2-D tables, and the basics of indexing and selection.

item.title: Object Instantiation
item.description: Classes contain not just methods but also data. We instantiate them as objects, distinguish static from instance methods, and meet Java's Lists, Maps, and fixed-size Arrays.
